48/// Settings that should be applied when creating a PDF document.
49#[derive(Clone, Debug)]
50pub struct SerializeSettings {
51    /// Whether to write PDFs in a way that is easier to inspect manually. This
52    /// will result in larger file sizes.
53    pub pretty: bool,
54    /// Whether content streams should be compressed. Leads to significantly smaller file sizes,
55    /// but also longer running times. It is highly recommended that you set this to `true`.
56    pub compress_content_streams: bool,
57    /// Whether device-independent colors should be used instead of
58    /// device-dependent ones.
59    ///
60    /// Note that this value might be overridden depending on which validator
61    /// you use. For example, when exporting to PDF/A, this value will be set to
62    /// true, regardless of what value will be passed.
63    pub no_device_cs: bool,
64    /// Whether the PDF should be ASCII-compatible, i.e. only consist of
65    /// characters in the ASCII range.
66    ///
67    /// Note that this only on a best-effort basis. For example, XMP metadata always
68    /// contains a binary marker. In addition to that, some validators,
69    /// like PDF/A, require that the file header be a binary marker, meaning
70    /// that the header itself will not be ASCII-compatible. Finally, embedded PDFs will
71    /// be embedded as is and not re-encoded with ASCII-compatible encoding.
72    pub ascii_compatible: bool,
73    /// Whether the PDF should include XMP metadata.
74    ///
75    /// Note that this value might be overridden depending on which validator
76    /// you use. For example, when exporting to PDF/A, this value will be set to
77    /// true, regardless of what value will be passed.
78    pub xmp_metadata: bool,
79    /// The ICC profile that should be used for CMYK colors
80    /// when `no_device_cs` is enabled.
81    ///
82    /// This is usually not required, but it is for example required when exporting
83    /// to PDF/A and using a CMYK color, since they have to be device-independent.
84    pub cmyk_profile: Option<ICCProfile<4>>,
85    /// A validator and PDF version used for export.
86    ///
87    /// In case validation fails, export will fail, and a list of validation errors that
88    /// occurred will be returned instead of the PDF.
89    ///
90    /// **Important**: Make sure to carefully read the documentation of the [`validate`] module
91    /// before using this feature! Just setting a validator might not be enough to ensure that
92    /// your output conforms to the given standard, as some requirements are semantic in nature
93    /// and cannot possibly be verified by krilla!
94    ///
95    /// However, as long as you carefully read and follow the documentation,
96    /// you can be certain that the resulting document will conform to the standard (unless there
97    /// is a bug).
98    ///
99    /// [`validate`]: crate::third_party::krilla::configure::validate
100    pub configuration: Configuration,
101    /// Whether to enable the creation of tagged documents. See the module documentation
102    /// of [`tagging`] for more information about tagged PDF documents.
103    ///
104    /// Note that enabling this does not automatically make your documents tagged, as tagging implies
105    /// enriching the document with semantic information, which krilla cannot do
106    /// for you, since it's content-agnostic. All this setting does is to allow you
107    /// to dynamically disable tagging if you wish to do so. This allows you to write
108    /// your code primarily with tagging in mind, but still allows you to
109    /// disable it dynamically, without having to make any changes to your code.
110    ///
111    /// Note that this value might be overridden depending on which validator
112    /// you use. For example, when exporting with PDF/UA, this value will always
113    /// be set to `true`.
114    ///
115    /// [`tagging`]: crate::third_party::krilla::interchange::tagging
116    pub enable_tagging: bool,
117    /// A function that should be used to render SVG glyphs. If you don't need this, yu can
118    /// just use the default function which doesn't render them at all. If you do want this, it
119    /// is recommended that you use the function provided by the `krilla-svg` crate.
120    pub render_svg_glyph_fn: RenderSvgGlyphFn,
121    /// The color space in which transparency is blended.
122    ///
123    /// See [`GroupColorSpace`].
124    pub group_color_space: GroupColorSpace,
125    /// The printing condition the document is prepared for, written as a `GTS_PDFX`
126    /// output intent. See [`OutputIntent`].
127    pub output_intent: Option<OutputIntent>,
128    /// Whether the document has been trapped: `/Trapped` in the document information
129    /// dictionary and `pdf:Trapped` in the XMP metadata.
130    pub trapped: Option<Trapped>,
131    /// The PDF/X version the caller claims, such as `PDF/X-4`: `/GTS_PDFXVersion` in the
132    /// document information dictionary and `pdfxid:GTS_PDFXVersion` in the XMP metadata.
133    ///
134    /// krilla does not check PDF/X conformance; the caller does. PDF/A-1, -2 and -3 need an
135    /// extension schema for the XMP property, which krilla does not write, so export under
136    /// them fails with [`ValidationError::PdfxVersionWithoutExtensionSchema`].
137    pub pdfx_version: Option<String>,
138    /// The PDF/X conformance level the caller claims, such as `PDF/X-1a:2003`:
139    /// `/GTS_PDFXConformance` in the document information dictionary. PDF/X-1a and X-3
140    /// require it next to the version (`PDF/X-1:2003` for PDF/X-1a:2003); later parts
141    /// have no conformance key. It has no XMP property, so PDF 2.0 output omits it.
142    pub pdfx_conformance: Option<String>,
143}
144
145/// A CMYK printing condition, written as an `/OutputIntents` entry with `/S /GTS_PDFX`.
146///
147/// When a PDF/A validator is active, its `GTS_PDFA1` entry names the same profile and
148/// condition, because PDF/A requires all output intents to share one destination profile.
149#[derive(Clone, Debug, Hash, PartialEq, Eq)]
150pub struct OutputIntent {
151    /// The destination profile (`/DestOutputProfile`).
152    pub profile: ICCProfile<4>,
153    /// `/OutputConditionIdentifier`, such as `FOGRA39`, or `Custom`.
154    pub condition_identifier: String,
155    /// `/OutputCondition`: a human-readable description of the condition.
156    pub condition: Option<String>,
157    /// `/RegistryName`, such as `http://www.color.org`.
158    pub registry_name: Option<String>,
159    /// `/Info`: required by PDF/X when the identifier is not in the registry.
160    pub info: Option<String>,
161}
162
163/// The trapping state of a document.
164#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, Hash, PartialEq, Eq)]
165pub enum Trapped {
166    /// The document is fully trapped.
167    True,
168    /// The document has not been trapped.
169    False,
170    /// The document is partly trapped or the state is unknown.
171    Unknown,
172}

174/// The color space in which transparency groups blend.
175#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, Default, Hash, PartialEq, Eq)]
176pub enum GroupColorSpace {
177    /// Every transparency group gets an RGB `/CS` (DeviceRGB, or sRGB when
178    /// `no_device_cs` is set). Pages get no `/Group`. Suits screen output.
179    #[default]
180    Rgb,
181    /// Pages that use transparency get a page group with a CMYK `/CS`: DeviceCMYK, or the
182    /// [`SerializeSettings::cmyk_profile`] when `no_device_cs` is set. Content groups and
183    /// embedded PDF pages write no `/CS` and inherit it. Soft-mask groups, which have no
184    /// parent, name DeviceCMYK, or sGrey when `no_device_cs` is set. Pages without
185    /// transparency get no page group.
186    ///
187    /// With `no_device_cs` and no `cmyk_profile`, [`Document::finish`] fails with
188    /// [`KrillaError::MissingGroupCmykProfile`].
189    ///
190    /// [`Document::finish`]: crate::third_party::krilla::Document::finish
191    Cmyk,
192}

196impl SerializeSettings {
197    pub(crate) fn pdf_version(&self) -> PdfVersion {
198        self.configuration.version()
199    }
200
201    pub(crate) fn validators(&self) -> Validators {
202        self.configuration.validators()
203    }
204
205    /// Whether the document information dictionary carries print markers. Like the rest of
206    /// the dictionary, they are deprecated in PDF 2.0 and only written to XMP there.
207    pub(crate) fn has_print_info(&self, version: PdfVersion) -> bool {
208        version < PdfVersion::Pdf20 && (self.trapped.is_some() || self.pdfx_version.is_some() || self.pdfx_conformance.is_some())
209    }
210
211    pub(crate) fn write_print_info(&self, info: &mut DocumentInfo<'_>) {
212        if let Some(trapped) = self.trapped {
213            info.trapped(match trapped {
214                Trapped::True => TrappingStatus::Trapped,
215                Trapped::False => TrappingStatus::NotTrapped,
216                Trapped::Unknown => TrappingStatus::Unknown,
217            });
218        }
219        if let Some(version) = &self.pdfx_version {
220            info.pair(Name(b"GTS_PDFXVersion"), TextStr(version));
221        }
222        if let Some(conformance) = &self.pdfx_conformance {
223            info.pair(Name(b"GTS_PDFXConformance"), TextStr(conformance));
224        }
225    }
226
227    pub(crate) fn write_print_xmp(&self, xmp: &mut XmpWriter) {
228        match self.trapped {
229            Some(Trapped::True) => {
230                xmp.trapped(true);
231            }
232            Some(Trapped::False) => {
233                xmp.trapped(false);
234            }
235            // The Adobe PDF schema allows `Unknown`, which `XmpWriter::trapped` can't write.
236            // PDF/A-1 requires it to match the information dictionary.
237            Some(Trapped::Unknown) => {
238                xmp.element("Trapped", Namespace::AdobePdf).value("Unknown");
239            }
240            None => {}
241        }
242        if let Some(version) = &self.pdfx_version {
243            xmp.pdfx_version(version);
244        }
245    }
246
247    /// Whether the `/AF` key is supported, accounting for the PDF version and active standards.
248    pub(crate) fn supports_associated_files(&self) -> bool {
249        self.configuration.version().specifies_associated_files() || self.configuration.validators().specifies_associated_files()
250    }
251}

350/// The serializer context is more or less the core piece of krilla. It is passed around
351/// throughout pretty much the whole conversion process, and contains all mutable state
352/// that is needed when writing a PDF file. This includes for example:
353/// - Storing all chunks that are produced.
354/// - The mappings from OTF fonts to CID/Type 3 fonts.
355/// - Annotations used in the document.
356///   etc.
357pub(crate) struct SerializeContext {
358    /// An unfinished or failed page/surface must never serialize as a complete document.
359    pub(crate) poisoned: bool,
360    /// Where the first mesh gradient whose corner colors share no color space was drawn;
361    /// [`SerializeContext::finish`] fails with [`KrillaError::MixedMeshColorSpaces`].
362    pub(crate) mixed_mesh_colors: Option<Option<Location>>,
363    /// The document's optional content groups.
364    pub(crate) optional_content: OptionalContent,
365    /// The ref of the page tree.
366    page_tree_ref: Ref,
367    /// PDF 2.0 namespaces.
368    pub(crate) pdf2_ns: Pdf2Namespaces,
369    /// All global objects, such as PDF fonts, that are populated over time.
370    pub(crate) global_objects: GlobalObjects,
371    /// Information for each page written so far, index by the page index.
372    page_infos: Vec<PageInfo>,
373    /// Keep track of object hashes and their corresponding reference. This is used for
374    /// caching, so that for example same images will not be embedded twice in the document.
375    cached_mappings: HashMap<u128, Ref>,
376    /// The current ref in use. All serializers should use the `new_ref` method (which indirectly
377    /// is based on this field) to generate a new Ref, instead of creating one manually with
378    /// `Ref::new`.
379    pub(crate) cur_ref: Ref,
380    /// All validation errors that are collected as part of the export process
381    /// alongside the validators that raised the error.
382    validation_errors: Vec<(ValidationError, Validators)>,
383    /// Settings used for serialization.
384    serialize_settings: Arc<SerializeSettings>,
385    /// Settings used for all PDF object chunks.
386    chunk_settings: Settings,
387    /// The limits created as part of the serialization process. In principle, we could
388    /// just keep track of this in `ChunkContainer`, where all used chunks are stored.
389    /// The only reason why `SerializeContext` needs to know about them is that we also
390    /// need to merge limits from postscript functions, which are not directly accessible
391    /// from the chunk they are written to.
392    limits: Limits,
393    /// Additional information stored during serialization that allows us to
394    /// raise standards errors later.
395    validation_store: ValidationStore,
396    /// The current location, if set.
397    pub(crate) location: Option<Location>,
398    /// Objects whose use makes a page blend: transparent graphics states, groups, images
399    /// with alpha, and forms, patterns and Type 3 fonts that use any of these. Decides
400    /// which pages get a page group under [`GroupColorSpace::Cmyk`]. Cached objects are
401    /// serialized once, so this is tracked by reference instead of by location.
402    transparent_refs: HashSet<Ref>,
403}
404
405impl SerializeContext {
406    pub(crate) fn new(mut serialize_settings: SerializeSettings) -> Self {
407        // Override flags as required by the validator
408        serialize_settings.no_device_cs |= serialize_settings.validators().requires_no_device_cs();
409        serialize_settings.enable_tagging |= serialize_settings.validators().requires_tagging();
410        serialize_settings.xmp_metadata |= serialize_settings.validators().requires_xmp_metadata();
411
412        let mut cur_ref = Ref::new(1);
413        let page_tree_ref = cur_ref.bump();
414        let pdf2_ns = Pdf2Namespaces { ssn_ref: cur_ref.bump(), krilla_ref: cur_ref.bump() };
415
416        let chunk_settings = Settings { pretty: serialize_settings.pretty };
417
418        Self {
419            poisoned: false,
420            mixed_mesh_colors: None,
421            optional_content: OptionalContent::default(),
422            cached_mappings: HashMap::new(),
423            pdf2_ns,
424            global_objects: GlobalObjects::default(),
425            cur_ref,
426            page_tree_ref,
427            page_infos: vec![],
428            location: None,
429            validation_errors: vec![],
430            serialize_settings: Arc::new(serialize_settings),
431            chunk_settings,
432            limits: Limits::new(),
433            validation_store: ValidationStore::new(),
434            transparent_refs: HashSet::new(),
435        }
436    }
437
438    /// Record that drawing `object` involves transparency.
439    pub(crate) fn mark_transparent(&mut self, object: Ref) {
440        self.transparent_refs.insert(object);
441    }
442
443    /// Whether content using `resources` involves transparency.
444    pub(crate) fn uses_transparency(&self, resources: &ResourceDictionary) -> bool {
445        resources
446            .ext_g_states
447            .refs()
448            .chain(resources.x_objects.refs())
449            .chain(resources.patterns.refs())
450            .chain(resources.fonts.refs())
451            .any(|r| self.transparent_refs.contains(&r))
452    }
453
454    /// The CMYK blending color space for page groups under [`GroupColorSpace::Cmyk`]. Falls back to DeviceCMYK when `no_device_cs` is set
455    /// without a CMYK profile; `finish` rejects that configuration.
456    pub(crate) fn cmyk_group_color_space(&mut self, chunk_container: &mut ChunkContainer) -> MaybeDeviceColorSpace {
457        let cs = cmyk::color_space(&self.serialize_settings).unwrap_or_else(|| DeviceColorSpace::Cmyk.into());
458        self.register_colorspace(chunk_container, cs.into())
459    }
460
461    /// The blending color space of soft-mask groups under [`GroupColorSpace::Cmyk`]:
462    /// DeviceCMYK, or sGrey when `no_device_cs` is set. A mask group has no parent, so it
463    /// need not match the page group. An ICC CMYK mask group would give the default black
464    /// backdrop a luminosity above 0, because 100% black through a CMYK profile is not black,
465    /// and the masked object would show where the mask content paints nothing.
466    pub(crate) fn mask_group_color_space(&mut self, chunk_container: &mut ChunkContainer) -> MaybeDeviceColorSpace {
467        if self.serialize_settings.no_device_cs {
468            self.register_colorspace(chunk_container, luma::color_space(true).into())
469        } else {
470            self.cmyk_group_color_space(chunk_container)
471        }
472    }
473
474    pub(crate) fn page_infos(&self) -> &[PageInfo] {
475        &self.page_infos
476    }
477
478    pub(crate) fn page_infos_mut(&mut self) -> &mut [PageInfo] {
479        &mut self.page_infos
480    }
481
482    pub(crate) fn set_outline(&mut self, outline: Outline) {
483        // Only set it if it's not empty or if the current validator requires an
484        // outline.
485        if !outline.is_empty() || self.serialize_settings.validators().prohibits(&ValidationError::MissingDocumentOutline).is_some() {
486            self.global_objects.outline = MaybeTaken::new(Some(outline));
487        }
488    }
489
490    pub(crate) fn set_location(&mut self, location: Location) {
491        self.location = Some(location)
492    }
493
494    pub(crate) fn reset_location(&mut self) {
495        self.location = None
496    }
497
498    pub(crate) fn embed_file(&mut self, chunk_container: &mut ChunkContainer, file: EmbeddedFile) -> Option<()> {
499        let name = file.path.clone();
500        let ref_ = self.register_cacheable(chunk_container, file);
501        if self.global_objects.embedded_files.insert(name, ref_).is_some() { None } else { Some(()) }
502    }
503
504    pub(crate) fn set_tag_tree(&mut self, root: TagTree) {
505        // Only set the tag tree if the user actually enabled tagging.
506        if self.serialize_settings.enable_tagging {
507            self.global_objects.tag_tree = MaybeTaken::new(Some(root))
508        }
509    }
510
511    pub(crate) fn new_ref(&mut self) -> Ref {
512        self.cur_ref.bump()
513    }
514
515    pub(crate) fn serialize_settings(&self) -> Arc<SerializeSettings> {
516        self.serialize_settings.clone()
517    }
518
519    // IMPORTANT: DO NEVER CALL `Chunk::new`, `Pdf::new` or `Content::new` directly! Instead,
520    // always make sure to use the methods on `SerializeContext`, to ensure the
521    // flags are applied consistently across all chunks.
522
523    pub(crate) fn new_chunk(&self) -> Chunk {
524        Chunk::with_settings(self.chunk_settings)
525    }
526
527    pub(crate) fn new_content(&self) -> Content {
528        Content::with_settings(self.chunk_settings)
529    }

531    pub(crate) fn new_pdf_with_capacity(&self, capacity: usize) -> Pdf {
532        Pdf::with_settings_and_capacity(self.chunk_settings, capacity)
533    }

535    #[cfg(any())]
536    pub(crate) fn chunk_settings(&self) -> Settings {
537        self.chunk_settings
538    }

540    #[cfg(any())]
541    pub(crate) fn embed_pdf_pages(&mut self, pdf: &PdfDocument, page_indices: &[usize]) {
542        for page_idx in page_indices {
543            let page_ref = self.new_ref();
544            let size = pdf
545                .pages()
546                .get(*page_idx)
547                .and_then(|p| {
548                    let (x, y) = p.render_dimensions();
549                    Size::from_wh(x, y)
550                })
551                // In case the page doesn't exist, we will catch the error later, so just use
552                // a dummy size.
553                .unwrap_or(Size::from_wh(1.0, 1.0).unwrap());
554            self.global_objects.pdf_ctx.add_page(pdf, *page_idx, page_ref, self.location);
555            self.page_infos.push(PageInfo::Pdf {
556                ref_: page_ref,
557                size,
558                // TODO: Maybe this should be configurable.
559                page_label: PageLabel::default(),
560            });
561        }
562    }
563
564    #[cfg(any())]
565    pub(crate) fn embed_pdf_page_as_xobject(&mut self, pdf: &PdfDocument, page_idx: usize) -> Ref {
566        let xobj_ref = self.new_ref();
567
568        // Note that `add_xobject` might return a different ref than the one we created.
569        let xobj_ref = self.global_objects.pdf_ctx.add_xobject(pdf, page_idx, xobj_ref, self.location);
570        // Embedded pages are always drawn as isolated transparency groups.
571        self.mark_transparent(xobj_ref);
572        xobj_ref
573    }
574
575    pub(crate) fn page_tree_ref(&mut self) -> Ref {
576        self.page_tree_ref
577    }
578
579    pub(crate) fn register_font_container(&mut self, font: Font) -> Rc<RefCell<FontContainer>> {
580        self.global_objects.font_map.entry(font.clone()).or_insert_with(|| Rc::new(RefCell::new(FontContainer::new(font.clone())))).clone()
581    }
582
583    pub(crate) fn validation_store(&mut self) -> &mut ValidationStore {
584        &mut self.validation_store
585    }
586
587    pub(crate) fn finish(mut self, mut chunk_container: ChunkContainer) -> KrillaResult<Pdf> {
588        let settings = &self.serialize_settings;
589        if settings.group_color_space == GroupColorSpace::Cmyk && settings.no_device_cs && settings.cmyk_profile.is_none() {
590            return Err(KrillaError::MissingGroupCmykProfile);
591        }
592        if self.serialize_settings.pdfx_version.is_some() {
593            self.register_validation_error(ValidationError::PdfxVersionWithoutExtensionSchema);
594        }
595        if let Some(location) = self.mixed_mesh_colors {
596            return Err(KrillaError::MixedMeshColorSpaces(location));
597        }
598        if let Some(location) = self.optional_content.misuse {
599            return Err(KrillaError::UnbalancedOptionalContent(location));
600        }
601
602        // We need to be careful here that we serialize the objects in the right order,
603        // as in some cases we use MaybeTake::take to remove an object, which means that
604        // no object that is serialized afterwards must depend on it.
605
606        // Serialize all objects that can only be written in the end.
607        self.serialize_destination_profiles(&mut chunk_container);
608        self.serialize_page_label_tree(&mut chunk_container);
609        self.serialize_outline(&mut chunk_container);
610        self.serialize_fonts(&mut chunk_container)?;
611        self.serialize_pages(&mut chunk_container)?;
612        self.serialize_page_tree(&mut chunk_container);
613        #[cfg(any())]
614        self.serialize_embedded_pdfs(&mut chunk_container)?;
615        self.serialize_xyz_destinations(&mut chunk_container)?;
616        // It is important that we serialize the tags AFTER we have serialized the pages,
617        // because page serialization will update the annotation refs of the page infos,
618        // and when serializing the parent tree map we need to know the refs of the annotations
619        self.serialize_tag_tree(&mut chunk_container)?;
620
621        // Create the final PDF.
622        let pdf = chunk_container.finish(&mut self)?;
623        self.register_limits(pdf.limits());
624
625        self.check_validator_limits();
626
627        if !self.validation_errors.is_empty() {
628            // Deduplicate errors, while still preserving order.
629            let mut errors = vec![];
630            let mut seen = HashSet::new();
631
632            for error in self.validation_errors {
633                if !seen.contains(&error) {
634                    seen.insert(error.clone());
635                    errors.push(error);
636                }
637            }
638
639            return Err(KrillaError::Validation(errors));
640        }
641
642        if let Some(limit_error) = self.check_version_limits() {
643            return Err(KrillaError::Limit(limit_error));
644        }
645
646        // Just a sanity check that we've actually processed all items.
647        self.global_objects.assert_all_taken();
648
649        Ok(pdf)
650    }
651}

653/// Various registration methods.
654impl SerializeContext {
655    pub(crate) fn register_validation_error(&mut self, error: ValidationError) {
656        if let Some(validators) = self.serialize_settings().validators().prohibits(&error) {
657            self.validation_errors.push((error, validators))
658        }
659    }
660
661    pub(crate) fn register_limits(&mut self, limits: &Limits) {
662        self.limits.merge(limits);
663    }
664
665    pub(crate) fn register_page_struct_parent(&mut self, page_index: usize, num_mcids: i32) -> Option<i32> {
666        if self.serialize_settings.enable_tagging {
667            if num_mcids == 0 {
668                return None;
669            }
670
671            let id = self.global_objects.struct_parents.len();
672            self.global_objects.struct_parents.push(StructParentElement::Page(page_index, num_mcids));
673            Some(i32::try_from(id).unwrap())
674        } else {
675            None
676        }
677    }
678
679    /// Register the struct parent integer in the parent tree.
680    /// The annotation parent must be later set using [`Self::set_annotation_parent`].
681    pub(crate) fn register_annotation_parent(&mut self, ai: AnnotationIdentifier) -> Option<i32> {
682        if self.serialize_settings.enable_tagging {
683            let id = self.global_objects.struct_parents.len();
684            self.global_objects.struct_parents.push(StructParentElement::Annotation(ai));
685            Some(i32::try_from(id).unwrap())
686        } else {
687            None
688        }
689    }
690
691    pub(crate) fn register_named_destination(&mut self, nd: NamedDestination) -> Option<Ref> {
692        if let Some((dest_ref, existing)) = self.global_objects.named_destinations.get(nd.name.as_ref()) {
693            return (existing == nd.xyz_dest.as_ref()).then_some(*dest_ref);
694        }
695
696        let dest_ref = self.register_xyz_destination((*nd.xyz_dest).clone());
697        self.global_objects.named_destinations.insert(nd.name.clone(), (dest_ref, (*nd.xyz_dest).clone()));
698        Some(dest_ref)
699    }
700
701    pub(crate) fn register_page(&mut self, page: InternalPage) {
702        let ref_ = self.new_ref();
703        self.page_infos.push(PageInfo::Krilla {
704            ref_,
705            surface_size: page.page_settings.surface_size(),
706            // Will be populated when the page is serialized.
707            annotations: vec![],
708            page_label: page.page_settings.page_label().clone(),
709        });
710        self.global_objects.pages.push((ref_, page));
711    }
712
713    fn register_cached<T: SipHashable>(&mut self, item: T, mut func: impl FnMut(&mut Self, T, Ref)) -> Ref {
714        let hash = item.sip_hash();
715        if let Some(_ref) = self.cached_mappings.get(&hash) {
716            *_ref
717        } else {
718            let root_ref = self.new_ref();
719            func(self, item, root_ref);
720            self.cached_mappings.insert(hash, root_ref);
721            root_ref
722        }
723    }
724
725    pub(crate) fn register_cacheable<T>(&mut self, chunk_container: &mut ChunkContainer, object: T) -> Ref
726    where
727        T: Cacheable,
728    {
729        self.register_cached(object, |sc, object, root_ref| {
730            object.serialize(sc, chunk_container, root_ref);
731        })
732    }
733
734    pub(crate) fn register_resourceable<T>(&mut self, chunk_container: &mut ChunkContainer, object: T) -> T::Resource
735    where
736        T: Resourceable,
737    {
738        Resource::new(self.register_cacheable(chunk_container, object))
739    }
740
741    pub(crate) fn register_image(&mut self, chunk_container: &mut ChunkContainer, image: Image) -> Ref {
742        self.register_cached(image, |sc, object, root_ref| {
743            object.serialize(sc, chunk_container, root_ref);
744        })
745    }
746
747    pub(crate) fn register_xyz_destination(&mut self, dest: XyzDestination) -> Ref {
748        self.register_cached(dest, |sc, dest, root_ref| {
749            sc.global_objects.xyz_destinations.push((root_ref, dest));
750        })
751    }
752
753    pub(crate) fn register_page_label(&mut self, chunk_container: &mut ChunkContainer, page_label: PageLabel) -> Ref {
754        let ref_ = self.new_ref();
755        page_label.serialize(chunk_container, ref_);
756        ref_
757    }
758
759    pub(crate) fn register_font_identifier(&mut self, f: FontIdentifier) -> resource::Font {
760        let hash = f.sip_hash();
761        if let Some(_ref) = self.cached_mappings.get(&hash) {
762            resource::Font::new(*_ref)
763        } else {
764            let root_ref = self.new_ref();
765            self.cached_mappings.insert(hash, root_ref);
766            resource::Font::new(root_ref)
767        }
768    }
769
770    pub(crate) fn register_colorspace(&mut self, chunk_container: &mut ChunkContainer, cs: ColorSpace) -> MaybeDeviceColorSpace {
771        match cs {
772            ColorSpace::CieBased(CieBasedColorSpace::Srgb) => MaybeDeviceColorSpace::ColorSpace(
773                self.register_resourceable(chunk_container, ICCBasedColorSpace(self.serialize_settings.pdf_version().rgb_icc())),
774            ),
775            ColorSpace::CieBased(CieBasedColorSpace::Luma) => MaybeDeviceColorSpace::ColorSpace(
776                self.register_resourceable(chunk_container, ICCBasedColorSpace(self.serialize_settings.pdf_version().grey_icc())),
777            ),
778            ColorSpace::CieBased(CieBasedColorSpace::Cmyk(cs)) => MaybeDeviceColorSpace::ColorSpace(self.register_resourceable(chunk_container, cs)),
779            ColorSpace::Device(DeviceColorSpace::Gray) => MaybeDeviceColorSpace::DeviceGray,
780            ColorSpace::Device(DeviceColorSpace::Rgb) => MaybeDeviceColorSpace::DeviceRgb,
781            ColorSpace::Device(DeviceColorSpace::Cmyk) => MaybeDeviceColorSpace::DeviceCMYK,
782            ColorSpace::Special(SpecialColorSpace::Separation(s)) => {
783                MaybeDeviceColorSpace::ColorSpace(self.register_resourceable(chunk_container, SeparationColorSpace::new(s)))
784            }
785            ColorSpace::Special(SpecialColorSpace::DeviceN(s)) => {
786                MaybeDeviceColorSpace::ColorSpace(self.register_resourceable(chunk_container, DeviceNColorSpace::new(s)))
787            }
788        }
789    }
790}

792/// Various serialization methods.
793/// All methods are supposed to only be called once in `SerializeContext::finish`!
794impl SerializeContext {
795    fn serialize_destination_profiles(&mut self, chunk_container: &mut ChunkContainer) {
796        let validators = self.serialize_settings.validators();
797        let pdfa = validators.output_intent();
798        let print = self.serialize_settings.output_intent.clone();
799        if pdfa.is_none() && print.is_none() {
800            return;
801        }
802
803        let root_ref = self.new_ref();
804        let mut chunk = self.new_chunk();
805        let mut intents = Vec::new();
806
807        if let Some(print) = print {
808            let profile_ref = self.register_cacheable(chunk_container, print.profile.clone());
809            for subtype in pdfa.into_iter().chain([OutputIntentSubtype::PDFX]) {
810                let oi_ref = self.new_ref();
811                let mut oi = chunk.indirect(oi_ref).start::<OutputIntentWriter>();
812                oi.dest_output_profile(profile_ref).subtype(subtype).output_condition_identifier(TextStr(&print.condition_identifier));
813                if let Some(condition) = &print.condition {
814                    oi.output_condition(TextStr(condition));
815                }
816                if let Some(registry_name) = &print.registry_name {
817                    oi.registry_name(TextStr(registry_name));
818                }
819                if let Some(info) = &print.info {
820                    oi.info(TextStr(info));
821                }
822                oi.finish();
823                intents.push(oi_ref);
824            }
825        } else if let Some(subtype) = pdfa {
826            let oi_ref = self.new_ref();
827            let mut oi = chunk.indirect(oi_ref).start::<OutputIntentWriter>();
828            let icc_profile = self.serialize_settings.pdf_version().rgb_icc();
829
830            oi.dest_output_profile(self.register_cacheable(chunk_container, icc_profile.clone()))
831                .subtype(subtype)
832                .output_condition_identifier(TextStr("Custom"))
833                .output_condition(TextStr("sRGB"))
834                .registry_name(TextStr(""))
835                .info(TextStr(format!("sRGB v{}.{}", icc_profile.metadata().major, icc_profile.metadata().minor).as_str()));
836            oi.finish();
837            intents.push(oi_ref);
838        }
839
840        chunk.indirect(root_ref).array().items(intents);
841        chunk_container.non_stream.destination_profiles = Some((root_ref, chunk));
842    }
843
844    fn serialize_page_label_tree(&mut self, chunk_container: &mut ChunkContainer) {
845        if let Some(container) = PageLabelContainer::new(&self.page_infos.iter().map(|page| page.page_label().clone()).collect::<Vec<_>>()) {
846            let page_label_tree_ref = self.new_ref();
847            container.serialize(self, chunk_container, page_label_tree_ref);
848        }
849    }
850
851    fn serialize_outline(&mut self, chunk_container: &mut ChunkContainer) {
852        let outline = self.global_objects.outline.take();
853        if let Some(outline) = &outline {
854            let outline_ref = self.new_ref();
855            outline.serialize(self, chunk_container, outline_ref);
856        } else {
857            self.register_validation_error(ValidationError::MissingDocumentOutline);
858        }
859    }
860
861    #[cfg(any())]
862    fn serialize_embedded_pdfs(&mut self, chunk_container: &mut ChunkContainer) -> KrillaResult<()> {
863        let pdf_ctx = self.global_objects.pdf_ctx.take();
864
865        pdf_ctx.serialize(self, chunk_container)
866    }
867
868    fn serialize_fonts(&mut self, chunk_container: &mut ChunkContainer) -> KrillaResult<()> {
869        let fonts = self.global_objects.font_map.take();
870        for font_container in fonts.values() {
871            let borrowed = font_container.borrow();
872
873            if !borrowed.type3_mapper().is_empty() {
874                for t3_font in borrowed.type3_mapper().fonts() {
875                    let f = self.register_font_identifier(t3_font.identifier());
876                    t3_font.serialize(self, chunk_container, f.get_ref());
877                }
878            }
879
880            if !borrowed.cid_font().is_empty() {
881                let f = self.register_font_identifier(borrowed.cid_font().identifier());
882                borrowed.cid_font().serialize(self, chunk_container, f.get_ref())?;
883            }
884        }
885
886        Ok(())
887    }
888
889    fn serialize_pages(&mut self, chunk_container: &mut ChunkContainer) -> KrillaResult<()> {
890        let pages = self.global_objects.pages.take();
891        for (ref_, page) in pages {
892            page.serialize(self, chunk_container, ref_)?;
893        }
894
895        Ok(())
896    }
897
898    fn serialize_page_tree(&mut self, chunk_container: &mut ChunkContainer) {
899        let mut page_tree_chunk = self.new_chunk();
900        page_tree_chunk.pages(self.page_tree_ref).count(self.page_infos.len() as i32).kids(self.page_infos.iter().map(|i| i.ref_()));
901        chunk_container.non_stream.page_tree = Some((self.page_tree_ref, page_tree_chunk));
902    }
903
904    fn serialize_xyz_destinations(&mut self, chunk_container: &mut ChunkContainer) -> KrillaResult<()> {
905        let xyz_destinations = self.global_objects.xyz_destinations.take();
906        for (ref_, dest) in &xyz_destinations {
907            dest.serialize(self, chunk_container, *ref_)?;
908        }
909
910        Ok(())
911    }
912
913    fn serialize_tag_tree(&mut self, chunk_container: &mut ChunkContainer) -> KrillaResult<()> {
914        let tag_tree = self.global_objects.tag_tree.take();
915        let struct_parents = self.global_objects.struct_parents.take();
916        if let Some(root) = &tag_tree {
917            let mut parent_tree_map = HashMap::new();
918            let mut id_tree_map = BTreeMap::new();
919            let struct_tree_root_ref = self.new_ref();
920            let document_ref = root.serialize(self, chunk_container, &mut parent_tree_map, &mut id_tree_map, struct_tree_root_ref)?;
921
922            root.validate(&id_tree_map)?;
923
924            let mut chunk = self.new_chunk();
925            let mut tree = chunk.indirect(struct_tree_root_ref).start::<StructTreeRoot>();
926
927            let mut sub_chunks = vec![];
928
929            if self.serialize_settings.pdf_version() < PdfVersion::Pdf20 {
930                let mut role_map = tree.role_map();
931                // Custom structure elements.
932                role_map.insert(Name(b"Datetime"), StructRole::Span);
933                role_map.insert(Name(b"Terms"), StructRole::Part);
934
935                // PDF 2.0 exclusive structure elements.
936                role_map.insert(Name(b"Title"), StructRole::P);
937                role_map.insert(Name(b"Strong"), StructRole::Span);
938                role_map.insert(Name(b"Em"), StructRole::Span);
939                for level in self.global_objects.custom_heading_roles.iter() {
940                    let role2 = StructRole2::Heading(*level);
941                    role_map.insert(role2.to_name(&mut [0; 6]), StructRole::P);
942                }
943            } else {
944                let mut namespaces = tree.namespaces();
945
946                // PDF 2.0 standard structure namespace
947                namespaces.item(self.pdf2_ns.ssn_ref);
948                let mut ns_chunk = self.new_chunk();
949                ns_chunk.namespace(self.pdf2_ns.ssn_ref).pdf_2_ns();
950                sub_chunks.push(ns_chunk);
951
952                // Custom krilla namspace
953                namespaces.item(self.pdf2_ns.krilla_ref);
954                let mut ns_chunk = self.new_chunk();
955                let mut ns = ns_chunk.namespace(self.pdf2_ns.krilla_ref);
956                ns.ns(TextStr("https://github.com/LaurenzV/krilla"));
957
958                // Custom structure elements.
959                ns.role_map_ns().to_pdf_2_0(Name(b"Datetime"), StructRole2::Span, self.pdf2_ns.ssn_ref).to_pdf_2_0(
960                    Name(b"Terms"),
961                    StructRole2::Part,
962                    self.pdf2_ns.ssn_ref,
963                );
964
965                ns.finish();
966                sub_chunks.push(ns_chunk);
967            }
968            tree.children().item(document_ref);
969
970            if !struct_parents.is_empty() {
971                let mut parent_tree = tree.parent_tree();
972                let mut tree_nums = parent_tree.nums();
973
974                for (index, struct_parent) in struct_parents.iter().enumerate() {
975                    match *struct_parent {
976                        StructParentElement::Page(page_index, num_mcids) => {
977                            let mut list_chunk = self.new_chunk();
978                            let list_ref = self.new_ref();
979
980                            let mut refs = list_chunk.indirect(list_ref).array();
981
982                            for mcid in 0..num_mcids {
983                                let rci = PageTagIdentifier::new(page_index, mcid);
984                                refs.item(
985                                    parent_tree_map
986                                        .get(&rci.into())
987                                        .unwrap_or_else(|| panic!("page tag identifier {rci:?} doesn't appear in the tag tree")),
988                                );
989                            }
990
991                            refs.finish();
992
993                            sub_chunks.push(list_chunk);
994                            tree_nums.insert(index as i32, list_ref);
995                        }
996                        StructParentElement::Annotation(ai) => {
997                            // Write a reference to the parent structure element.
998                            // From the PDF 1.7 spec (14.7.5.4 Finding structure elements from content items):
999                            // > For an object identified as a content item by means of an object reference
1000                            // > (see 14.7.5.3, "PDF objects as content items"), the value shall be an
1001                            // > indirect reference to the parent structure element.
1002                            let page_annotations = &self.page_infos[ai.page_index].annotations();
1003                            let parent_ref = *page_annotations[ai.annot_index]
1004                                .1
1005                                .get()
1006                                .unwrap_or_else(|| panic!("annotation identifier {ai:?} doesn't appear in the tag tree"));
1007                            tree_nums.insert(index as i32, parent_ref);
1008                        }
1009                    }
1010                }
1011
1012                tree_nums.finish();
1013                parent_tree.finish();
1014            }
1015
1016            if !id_tree_map.is_empty() {
1017                let mut id_tree = tree.id_tree();
1018                let mut names = id_tree.names();
1019
1020                for (name, ref_) in id_tree_map {
1021                    names.insert(Str(name.as_bytes()), ref_);
1022                }
1023            }
1024
1025            if !struct_parents.is_empty() {
1026                tree.parent_tree_next_key(struct_parents.len() as i32);
1027            }
1028            tree.finish();
1029
1030            for sub_chunk in sub_chunks {
1031                chunk.extend(&sub_chunk);
1032            }
1033
1034            chunk_container.non_stream.struct_tree_root = Some((struct_tree_root_ref, chunk));
1035        } else {
1036            self.register_validation_error(ValidationError::MissingTagging);
1037        }
1038
1039        Ok(())
1040    }
1041
1042    fn check_validator_limits(&mut self) {
1043        if self.cur_ref > Ref::new(8388607) {
1044            self.register_validation_error(ValidationError::TooManyIndirectObjects)
1045        }
1046
1047        if self.limits.str_len() > STR_LEN {
1048            self.register_validation_error(ValidationError::TooLongString);
1049        }
1050
1051        if self.limits.name_len() > NAME_LEN {
1052            self.register_validation_error(ValidationError::TooLongName);
1053        }
1054
1055        if self.limits.real() > MAX_FLOAT {
1056            self.register_validation_error(ValidationError::TooLargeFloat);
1057        }
1058
1059        if self.limits.array_len() > ARRAY_LEN {
1060            self.register_validation_error(ValidationError::TooLongArray);
1061        }
1062
1063        if self.limits.dict_entries() > DICT_LEN {
1064            self.register_validation_error(ValidationError::TooLongDictionary);
1065        }
1066    }
1067
1068    fn check_version_limits(&self) -> Option<LimitError> {
1069        if self.serialize_settings.pdf_version() != PdfVersion::Pdf14 {
1070            return None;
1071        }
1072
1073        if self.limits.real() > MAX_FLOAT {
1074            return Some(LimitError::TooLargeFloat);
1075        }
1076
1077        if self.limits.array_len() > ARRAY_LEN {
1078            return Some(LimitError::TooLongArray);
1079        }
1080
1081        if self.limits.dict_entries() > DICT_LEN {
1082            return Some(LimitError::TooLongDictionary);
1083        }
1084
1085        None
1086    }
1087}
1088
1089/// This struct is essentially a thin wrapper around `std::mem::replace`. When finishing the
1090/// document, we need to take ownership of many of the items in `GlobalObjects` in order to
1091/// prevent having to clone them. However, the problem is that we cannot easily take ownership
1092/// of them, because they are part of the SerializeContext. Because of this, what we
1093/// do is that we `std::mem::replace` the elements step by step and then serialize them.
1094/// The `MaybeTaken` struct helps us to ensure that once we have taken a value, we do not
1095/// accidentally attempt to write/read it again.
1096pub(crate) struct MaybeTaken<T>(Option<T>);
1097
1098impl<T> MaybeTaken<T> {
1099    pub(crate) fn new(item: T) -> Self {
1100        Self(Some(item))
1101    }
1102
1103    pub(crate) fn is_taken(&self) -> bool {
1104        self.0.is_none()
1105    }
1106}
1107
1108impl<T> MaybeTaken<T> {
1109    #[track_caller]
1110    pub(crate) fn take(&mut self) -> T {
1111        self.0.take().expect("value was already taken before")
1112    }
1113}
1114
1115impl<T: Default> Default for MaybeTaken<T> {
1116    fn default() -> Self {
1117        Self::new(T::default())
1118    }
1119}
1120
1121impl<T> Deref for MaybeTaken<T> {
1122    type Target = T;
1123
1124    #[track_caller]
1125    fn deref(&self) -> &Self::Target {
1126        self.0.as_ref().expect("value was taken")
1127    }
1128}
1129
1130impl<T> DerefMut for MaybeTaken<T> {
1131    #[track_caller]
1132    fn deref_mut(&mut self) -> &mut Self::Target {
1133        self.0.as_mut().expect("value was taken")
1134    }
1135}

1144#[derive(Default)]
1145pub(crate) struct GlobalObjects {
1146    /// All named destinations that have been registered, including a Ref to their destination and
1147    /// the destination itself.
1148    // Needs to be pub(crate) because writing of named destinations happens in `ChunkContainer`.
1149    pub(crate) named_destinations: MaybeTaken<HashMap<Arc<String>, (Ref, XyzDestination)>>,
1150    /// A map from fonts to font container.
1151    font_map: MaybeTaken<IndexMap<Font, Rc<RefCell<FontContainer>>>>,
1152    /// All XYZ destinations used in the document. The reason we need to store them
1153    /// separately is that we can only serialize them in the very end, once all pages
1154    /// have been written, so that we know the Ref of the page they belong to.
1155    xyz_destinations: MaybeTaken<Vec<(Ref, XyzDestination)>>,
1156    /// All pages and their corresponding chunks. Similarly to destinations, they need
1157    /// to be written in the very end, because pages might contain annotations which in turn
1158    /// depend on future pages (not written yet), so pages must also only be written in the
1159    /// very end.
1160    pages: MaybeTaken<Vec<(Ref, InternalPage)>>,
1161    /// Stores the struct parent elements.
1162    struct_parents: MaybeTaken<Vec<StructParentElement>>,
1163    /// Stores the document outline.
1164    outline: MaybeTaken<Option<Outline>>,
1165    /// Stores the tag tree.
1166    tag_tree: MaybeTaken<Option<TagTree>>,
1167    /// Stores the association of the names of embedded files to their refs,
1168    /// for the catalog dictionary.
1169    pub(crate) embedded_files: MaybeTaken<BTreeMap<String, Ref>>,
1170    /// A list of custom headings numbers used in the document.
1171    pub(crate) custom_heading_roles: BTreeSet<NonZeroU16>,
1172    /// The context tracking all of the pdfs and their pages that have been inserted.
1173    #[cfg(any())]
1174    pub(crate) pdf_ctx: MaybeTaken<PdfSerializerContext>,
1175}
1176
1177impl GlobalObjects {
1178    pub(crate) fn assert_all_taken(&self) {
1179        assert!(self.named_destinations.is_taken());
1180        assert!(self.font_map.is_taken());
1181        assert!(self.xyz_destinations.is_taken());
1182        assert!(self.pages.is_taken());
1183        assert!(self.struct_parents.is_taken());
1184        assert!(self.outline.is_taken());
1185        assert!(self.tag_tree.is_taken());
1186        assert!(self.embedded_files.is_taken());
1187        #[cfg(any())]
1188        assert!(self.pdf_ctx.is_taken());
1189    }
1190}
